Cyber Attack Targets Philippine Semiconductor Firms, Disrupting Production and Operations

A cyber attack has severely disrupted operations across multiple semiconductor manufacturing firms in the Philippines, with several key sites still offline as of Tuesday afternoon. The attack, first detected late Sunday evening, has been described by industry sources as likely ransomware, though details of the perpetrators remain unconfirmed.

Affected companies, including TechSilicon Philippines, MicroFab Solutions, and AsiaSemicon Corp, have reported extensive outages in their IT systems, halting production lines and impeding administrative operations. “Our production control and quality assurance systems were rendered inaccessible almost immediately,” said an executive at MicroFab Solutions, requesting anonymity. “We have had to suspend all output while we work to restore critical functions.”

Industry body Semiconductor Manufacturers Association of the Philippines (SMAP) stated that at least seven facilities in the Calabarzon and Clark regions are currently affected. Many sites have implemented emergency protocols, including manual security checks, to safeguard sensitive intellectual property and partially resume limited operations. However, SMAP warned that the disruption could last several days. “Our top priority is restoring systems safely and ensuring the well-being of our workforce,” said SMAP spokesperson Liza Santos.

Thousands of workers at plants hit by the attack have been instructed to remain on-site or at home until further notice, with some companies providing temporary support packages. “We have not received a timeline for when we can return to full operations,” said Jerome Diaz, a union representative at a Laguna-based facility. “The uncertainty is difficult for everyone.”

Cybersecurity analysts have noted the increasing frequency of such attacks in the region’s semiconductor sector, highlighting the need for stronger digital defenses. As recovery efforts continue, the industry remains on high alert, with ongoing assessments of potential data breaches and operational damage.
